harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10, using pg_basebackup with physical replication slots and a replicator role (password generated on-node and relayed node-to-node via cluster SSH keys, never exposed in the final report). Simulated primary loss by stopping PostgreSQL on node1, confirmed both standbys were fully caught up (no data-loss risk), promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote, repointed node3 to stream from node2, then rebuilt node1 from a fresh base backup of node2 and brought it back online as a standby. Verified zero committed-data loss throughout (all pre-failover rows plus new writes present on every node). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node3, node1, then node2/the primary last) using systemd reboot, proving each node's changed boot_id and confirming PostgreSQL, recovery state, and streaming replication/slots fully recovered after each restart, with a final cross-node row-count consistency check (5/5/5) after all restarts completed.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 on node1, node2, node3 from the RHEL10 AppStream repo
Initialized DB on node1, configured wal_level/max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots/hot_standby and pg_hba.conf for replication + client access
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes
Generated a replicator role password on node1 and relayed it to node2/node3 via direct node-to-node SSH using cluster-provided SSH keys (never printed in final output)
Created replicator role and a failover_demo test table with seed data on node1
Base-backed-up node2 and node3 from node1 with physical replication slots (node2_slot, node3_slot) after diagnosing and fixing an initial WAL-recycling failure from an unslotted backup
Verified streaming replication healthy on both standbys and live INSERT propagation
Simulated primary loss: stopped postgresql on node1, confirmed both standbys fully caught up on LSN
Promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote; verified prior committed rows intact plus new post-failover write accepted
Created replication slots on node2 (node1_slot, node3_slot) and pg_hba entries for its new standbys
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo/primary_slot_name to node2 and restarted it as a standby of node2; confirmed data caught up
Rebuilt node1 via pg_basebackup from node2 and brought it up as a standby of node2 with node1_slot
Verified full 3-node cluster health (node2 primary, node1+node3 streaming standbys, both slots active) and inserted+propagated a post-recovery row

Executed mandatory restart protocol sequentially on node3, then node1, then node2 (the current primary): captured boot_id + service/data health baseline, issued systemctl reboot backgrounded, polled until exec access returned, proved boot_id changed, and verified postgresql active, replication/recovery state, and data integrity after each restart
Ran a final cross-node consistency check (row count 5 on node1 and node3) after all three restarts completed

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication established: node1 primary, node2+node3 standbys
evidence.summary: node1 primary active with pg_stat_replication showing both node2 and node3 streaming with active slots; INSERT on node1 propagated to both standbys' failover_demo table

evidence.requirement: Primary loss handled: standby promotes to writable primary without losing committed data
evidence.summary: node1 stopped at LSN 0/703C778; both standbys confirmed caught up to 0/703C7F0 (past primary's last LSN); node2 promoted (pg_is_in_recovery=f) and shown to retain seed rows 1-2 plus accept a new write (id 35)

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary rejoins as standby of the new primary; surviving standby reparented
evidence.summary: node3 repointed to stream from node2 and shown to have all rows including the post-failover write; node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2 and brought up as standby; node2's pg_stat_replication shows both node1 and node3 streaming, and a new insert on node2 propagated to node1

evidence.requirement: Restart evidence: node3 (standby) boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 180a78a0...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 5c5af0ff... (changed); postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, all 4 rows intact, and node2 shows node3 reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: Restart evidence: node1 (standby) boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id aad96cc9...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 940b617f... (changed); postgresql active, standby recovered with all 4 rows, node2 shows both standbys streaming again

evidence.requirement: Restart evidence: node2 (current primary) boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6d37896c...; reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 362f38c4... (changed); postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=f (writable primary preserved), all 4 rows intact, both replication slots active and standbys reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster data consistency after all restarts
evidence.summary: Insert on node2 (primary) propagated; row count of 5 confirmed identical on node1 and node3 standbys
